references.raw_reference: Notes on contributors Ibtissam Lamoune is a Ph.D. researcher in the Department of Radio, Television, and Cinema at Ankara University, Türkiye. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Sound Engineering and a Master's degree in Techniques and Art of Image and Sound from the Higher Institute of Broadcasting and Cinema Professions (ISMAC) in Rabat, Morocco, where she also served as a visiting lecturer (professeur vacataire). Her research interests and publications focus on visual culture, film sociology, feminist film theory, and media discourse. Notes on contributors Ibtissam Lamoune is a Ph.D. researcher in the Department of Radio, Television, and Cinema at Ankara University, Türkiye. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Sound Engineering and a Master's degree in Techniques and Art of Image and Sound from the Higher Institute of Broadcasting and Cinema Professions (ISMAC) in Rabat, Morocco, where she also served as a visiting lecturer (professeur vacataire). Her research interests and publications focus on visual culture, film sociology, feminist film theory, and media discourse. Her work examines creative labor, women's spatial agency in contemporary Moroccan and Maghrebi cinema, cinematic critiques of urban modernity, and the media framing and securitization of North African immigration in European press narratives.
